True or False: There is an element of luck in chess.
True, but in a very small way. Assuming both players are perfect, whoever goes first will win... (true of tic-tac-toe and checkers), so whoever gets white at the beginning has an advantage.

True. In the game "ChessLuck." At the start of each turn, the player rolls a pair of dice. If doubles, the player has to move a power piece, else any move is permitted. This rule stands until either half of your pawns or half of your power pieces are left. Then it's normal chess. If one opponent still has more than half, the rules of ChessLuck apply to him only.

It sets up some great last moves.
There is another one called Dice Chess where each piece is assigned a number. You can only roll a number go a piece that has available moves. You can play that and many other variations at BrainKing.

Not in the traditional sense, but in a convoluted sort of a way, yeah, kind of. It is likely that there is a dominant strategy but possible chess is actually a very complex version of tic tac toe. If you're unfamiliar with the term it comes from game theory. A dominant strategy is one which employed cannot lose regardless of what the other player decides to do. That doesn't mean that you don't react to what the other player does but simply that you have a set of known moves based off the other player's moves that cannot result in a loss if followed correctly. The dominant strategy would most likely be enjoyed by the player who moves first.

As for the reality of the game at the current time, it would depend largely on the relative skills of the two players. With amateurs who are relatively unfamiliar with the deeper strategies of chess I think there is a fair amount of luck as the players don't really understand what they are doing. As familiarity with the game increases the element of luck diminishes as players are more familiar with the various strategies of the game.
